name: Shock-tube fertilizer maker
subtitle: farm nitrate made from air by shock waves

effects.effect: a shock wave heats air for a millionth of a second, then lets it cool at once
plants need nitrogen from the soil

effect: a shock wave heats air for a millionth of a second, then lets it cool at once
how: Nitrogen fertilizer is made in a few giant gas-burning plants and trucked to farms, so the poorest farmers pay the most for it. Lightning makes fertilizer from air by heating it until nitrogen and oxygen join; here a piston slams air into a shock wave that does the same for a millionth of a second, and the gas cools again so fast that the new compound can't fall apart. Bubbled through water, it becomes nitrate for the field.
obstacle: Only a few percent of the air turns into the compound, so the energy per kilogram is still far above a gas-fired plant's.
why: The flash-heat-then-quench recipe suits the chemistry; whether yields per joule can compete is open.
real: 1950s patent US2832665 proposes shock-tube heating plus rapid expansion quench for fixing atmospheric nitrogen as NO, and shock-tube N2+O2 kinetics are studied, but no fertilizer device was found.
